steps.name: Measure and apply the open-pore baseline
steps.proposal:
Noise (robust sigma)  
4.52 pA
Longest state  
499 ms (422 states)
Median state (base_s floor)  
20.7 ms -> base_s >= 100 ms
Pore stepping (gating)  
no -- 0.5x noise
Proposed rough window  
2 s
Proposed base window  
500 ms
Decimation (derived)  
333
Ranked: 1 s / 300 ms  
baseline follows NONE (0.000%) of the state depth at the median (239 states) but RIDES INTO a 473 ms state at t = 38.3 s, 55.6% of its excursion followed
Ranked: 2 s / 500 ms  
baseline follows NONE of the state depth (0.000%, 240 states; worst single state NONE (-11.2%)) — CHOSEN

Longest state 499 ms (422 states, 9.3% of the trace) -> the rule's rough window 2 s, so no single state fills more than ~33% of the window; no gating detected (0.5); shortest level dwell n/a -> the rule's base window 500 ms. RANKED BY MEASURED INTRUSION, on two criteria. The MEDIAN share of each state's own depth the tracked baseline follows is the same statistic Baseline health condemns above 3% of the state depth, from the same estimator; the WORST single state is measured beside it because one state ridden into cannot move a median over hundreds, and a window whose baseline follows more than 50% of any one state's excursion has ridden INTO that state and loses to any window that stays out. Measured here: 1 s / 300 ms follows NONE (0.000%) of each state's own depth at the MEDIAN, but RIDES INTO its worst single state -- 55.6% of a 473 ms state's own excursion followed, at t = 38.3 s -- which one state among 239 cannot move a median to show; 2 s / 500 ms follows NONE of each state's own depth (0.000%, i.e. its baseline sits at or just outside them) (worst single state NONE of its own excursion, -11.2%). Inside the 473 ms state that 1 s / 300 ms rides into, depths would be measured against a baseline that has followed 56% of the state itself -- a blockade that long can stop being detectable at all -- while at 2 s / 500 ms no single state is followed more than 0.0% of the way. 2 s / 500 ms is taken: it is the SHORTEST window ESTIMATED that scores best on both criteria -- riding into no state, then the lowest measured median intrusion. Shortest, because a longer window is not free -- it tracks slower drift less well -- so among windows that measure the same on both criteria the app takes the least smoothing it can get away with. No wider window was estimated: under this ranking's objective -- no state ridden into, then median intrusion, ties to the shortest window -- nothing WIDER can beat a window already clean on both criteria: it could at best match them and then lose the tie-break. That is a claim about the objective on the ladder walked, not a measurement of any window left unestimated. What could have beaten it is a SHORTER window that is equally clean on both criteria, and the search looked: the nearest one, 1 s / 300 ms, was estimated and RIDES INTO a 473 ms state (55.6% of its own excursion followed), so nothing shorter was taken. 2 shorter windows on the grid (0.3 s / 100 ms; 0.5 s / 100 ms) were NOT estimated -- intrusion grows, and riding deepens, as the tracking window shortens, which is measured and not proved, so this is where the search stops rather than a claim that they are worse. (1 wider window on the grid was not estimated at all: under the objective above it could at best match this window on both criteria and then lose the tie-break -- a stop rule, not a measurement of it.)
